source_text:
1 Thess 3,3 Οὐκ εἶπεν τὸ μηδένα ὀκλάζειν, ἵνα μὴ δόξῃ κατηγορεῖν, ἀλλ'
ἔθηκε λέξιν τὴν μὴ δυναμένην ἐλεγκτικὴν εἶναι τῆς ἐνδόσεως σαίνεσθαι εἰπὼν τὸ
μηδένα ξενίζεσθαι. 1 Thess 4,15®17 Οὐκ αὐτὸς ἔμελλε περιλιμπάνεσθαι, φησίν, ἀλλὰ
τὸ ἡμεῖς ἢ ἀντὶ τοῦ τοσοῦτον ὀλίγοι καὶ 330 εὐαρίθμητοι περιλειφθήσονται, οὐ
φθάσουσι τοὺς κεκοιμημένους ἁγίους εἰς τὴν ἀπάντησιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ· εἰ γὰρ καὶ
πάντες ἐγείρονται, ἀλλ' οὐ πάντες ἀπαντήσουσι τῷ Χριστῷ ἀλλ' οἱ δίκαιοι. δῆλον
οὖν ὅτι ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ζῶντές τινες καταλαμβάνονται. ἢ καὶ
τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν ὅ φησιν· εἰ συνέβαινε νῦν τὸν Χριστὸν ἐλθεῖν, ἡμεῖς οἱ
περιλιμπανόμενοι σήμερον οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τοὺς
κοιμηθέντας. στικτέον δὲ μετὰ τὸ οἱ περιλειπόμενοι εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ κυρίου οὐ μὴ
φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας. Ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου. τὸ αὐτὸ λέγει καὶ ὁ κύριος·
μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς φωνὴ ἐγένετο· ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος ἔρχεται. Καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐν Χριστῷ
ἀναστήσονται πρῶτον. τοῦτο πάλιν αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος λέγει ἐν τοῖς Εὐαγγελίοις, ὅθεν
καὶ ὁ κύριος καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολος αἰνίττονται ὅτι νυκτὸς ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ κυρίου.
Ἔπειτα ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι, ἀντὶ τοῦ οἱ 329, col 2 περὶ ἡμᾶς δίκαιοι.
Ζῶντας ἔτι τινὰς βούλεται καταλαμβάνεσθαι ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τοῦτο
δηλοῦσθαι 330,ξολ2 ἐκ τοῦ ἡμεῖς οἱ περιλειπόμενοι ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ κυρίου.
thought_title: Paul's wording about those left and the resurrection order
orientation: Severianus is explaining Paul's wording in 1 Thessalonians 3:3 and 4:15-17 about who will be left alive and who will rise first at Christ's coming.
pass_a_gloss: He did not say that no one should waver, lest he seem to accuse, but he set down a word that cannot be a refutation of the yielding, saying that no one should be disturbed. He himself was not going to be left behind, he says, but the 'we' is either instead of 'so few and easily counted will be left behind', they will not precede those who have fallen asleep, the saints, into the meeting of Christ; for even if all are raised, yet not all will meet Christ but the righteous. It is clear therefore that at the coming of Christ some living people are also overtaken. Or also what he says is of this sort: if it happened that Christ came now, we who are left behind today would certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep at the coming of Christ. And one must punctuate after 'those who are left': into the day of the Lord we will certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep. With a voice of an archangel. The Lord also says the same thing: and at midnight a voice came: behold the bridegroom comes. And the dead in Christ will rise first. This again the Lord himself says in the Gospels, from which both the Lord and the apostle hint that the coming of the Lord will be at night. Then we the living who are left, instead of 'the righteous around us'. He wants some still living to be overtaken at the coming of Christ, and this to be shown from 'we who are left at the coming of the Lord'.

choices.why: The verb σαίνω in this context means to be shaken or disturbed, matching the sense of ξενίζεσθαι that follows; the glossary does not cover it, so a plain sense rendering is used.
The glossary gives 'those who are left' for οἱ περιλειπόμενοι; the verb form here is rendered consistently as 'left behind' to preserve the same root sense.
The double negative οὐ μή with the aorist subjunctive expresses strong denial; 'certainly not' preserves the emphatic force.
The verb means to be caught or overtaken by an event; 'overtaken' fits the sudden coming of Christ and is used consistently for this verb in the passage.
The verbal adjective expresses necessity; 'one must punctuate' preserves the impersonal prescriptive force of the Greek.

pass_b_english: On “so that no one would be disturbed” (1 Thessalonians 3:3): he did not say “so that no one would waver,” lest he seem to be accusing them, but he chose a word that cannot serve as a reproof of their weakness when he said “so that no one would be disturbed.”

On “we who are left” (1 Thessalonians 4:15): he did not mean that he himself was going to be left behind, he says, but “we” stands for “so few and easily counted will be left that they will not precede those holy ones who have fallen asleep into the meeting with Christ.” For even if all are raised, not all will meet Christ, but only the righteous. It is clear, then, that at the coming of Christ some are overtaken while still living.

Or what he says is something like this: if it happened that Christ came now, we who are left today would certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep at the coming of Christ. One must punctuate after “we who are left”: “into the day of the Lord we will certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep.”
On “with the voice of an archangel” (1 Thessalonians 4:16): the Lord says the same thing: “At midnight there was a cry: Look, the bridegroom is coming” (Matthew 25:6).

“And the dead in Christ will rise first” (1 Thessalonians 4:16): again the Lord himself says this in the Gospels, which is why both the Lord and the apostle hint that the coming of the Lord will be at night.

“Then we who are alive, who are left” (1 Thessalonians 4:17): that is, the righteous around us. He wants it to be understood that some are still living and are overtaken at the coming of Christ, and this is made clear from “we who are left at the coming of the Lord.”

last_rejected.quote: the Lord says the same thing
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ αὐτὸ λέγει καὶ ὁ κύριος
last_rejected.why: The English 'the Lord says' could be clearer that this is Christ speaking per voices brief, but it's not wrong. Actually, re-reading: the voices brief says Christ's words are marked by 'ὁ κύριος λέγει ἐν τοῖς Εὐαγγελίοις' etc. Here we have 'τὸ αὐτὸ λέγει καὶ ὁ κύριος'. The English renders this as 'the Lord says the same thing'. This is accurate. Not a problem.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek τὸ αὐτὸ λέγει καὶ ὁ κύριος = 'the Lord also says the same'; English matches.
English includes 'today' matching σήμερον; no omission.

last_rejected.why: 'εὐαρίθμητοι' means 'easily counted' or 'few in number', but context suggests 'so few and easily counted' is okay. Actually this is fine.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐαρίθμητοι = 'easily counted' or 'few'; English rendering is accurate.
